title: Bounded-below enhanced etale derived descent on an open basis
statement:
Let $B$ be an arbitrary scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and $\mathcal B$ a set of open subschemes forming a basis: every point of every open $W\subseteq B$ lies in some $U\in\mathcal B$ with $U\subseteq W$. All categories and indexing sets are small in a sufficiently large fixed universe [def-weil-size-convention]. For an open $W$, write $\mathbf D(W_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ for the enhanced localization of complexes of constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves at quasi-isomorphisms: it retains derived mapping complexes, composition homotopies and their higher compatibilities. Its ordinary homotopy category is $D(W_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; write $\mathbf D^+$ for its full subcategory of objects with cohomology sheaves zero below some integer. Restriction is exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

A coherent cartesian basis system is a family $M_U\in\mathbf D(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ with equivalences $M_U|_V\simeq M_V$ for every inclusion $V\subseteq U$ of basis members, together with composition homotopies for every string of inclusions and all higher compatibilities. Morphisms and mapping complexes are those of the homotopy limit of this restriction diagram, including their matching homotopies. Let $\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ub}}(B,\mathcal B,\Lambda)$ be its full subcategory consisting of systems for which a single integer $a$ satisfies $\mathcal H^i(M_U)=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and $i<a$.

Restriction gives an equivalence of enhanced categories
$$\mathbf D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\simeq\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ub}}(B,\mathcal B,\Lambda).$$
It identifies the full subcategories with the prescribed lower bound $a$, for every integer $a$. These equivalences commute coherently with restriction to an arbitrary open $W\subseteq B$ (using the basis members contained in $W$) and with refinement of the basis. For any enhanced parameter category $P$ small in the chosen larger universe, restriction also induces an equivalence of functor categories
$$\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathbf D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ub}}(B,\mathcal B,\Lambda)).$$
The integer lower bound may depend on the object of $P$. This equivalence includes coherent natural transformations and their compositions, identities and homotopies; equations supplied as coherent diagrams descend to equations in the ordinary homotopy category. No faithfulness of the family of ordinary restriction functors on ordinary derived morphisms is asserted, and no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $B$ or of overlaps is assumed.

proof.text: Fix an integer $a$. For every open $U$, apply [lem-cbc-bounded-below-hypersheaf-model] to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. This represents $M_U$ by $F_U(T)=R\Gamma(T,M_U)$ and identifies the full lower-bound-$a$ subcategory with $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. These are small sites in the fixed enlarged universe. To obtain a strict inclusion diagram, use the full subcategory $\mathcal C_U\subseteq B_{\mathrm{et}}$ on objects whose structure maps factor through $U$: such a factorization is unique. The cited slice equivalence identifies it with $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, including the topology. For $V\subseteq U$, the site $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the slice of $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ at $V$; its inclusion is a full sieve because a morphism $T\to S$ over $U$ with $S$ over the open $V$ uniquely factors $T$ through $V$. Open immersions and their composites with etale maps are etale. The slice compatibility in the model lemma therefore identifies restriction of $F_U$ with the presheaf attached to $M_U|_V$. Module inverse image is exact, so the original lower bound is preserved. This gives a coherent identification of the entire basis diagram, before taking its limit.

proof.text: Form $\mathcal E$ with objects $(U,T\to U)$, $U\in\mathcal B$, and arrows $(V,T)\to(U,S)$ consisting of $V\subseteq U$ and a morphism $T\to S$ over $B$. Give it the topology generated by vertical etale covers and singleton identity-underlying arrows $(V,T)\to(U,T)$. For $p:\mathcal E\to B_{\mathrm{et}}$, $(U,T)\mapsto T$, a family with target $(U,T)$ is covering exactly when its underlying family covers $T$: each member $(V_i,T_i)$ may first be replaced by $(U,T_i)$, giving a vertical cover, then by its singleton identity-underlying arrow. Conversely the generators have covering images. For a pullback along $(W,S)\to(U,T)$, first take the vertical cover $\{S\times_TT_i\to S\}$ in $W_{\mathrm{et}}$; cover each member by its inverse images of basis opens $Z\subseteq W\cap V_i$. These refinements map to $(V_i,T_i)$ and use only vertical covers and singleton changes of label. Thus the described covering sieves are stable under pullback, and transitivity follows by composing the underlying etale covers. Each etale object $T\to B$ is covered by $T_U=T\times_B U$, $U\in\mathcal B$. Given $p(V,T)\to p(U,S)$, cover $T$ by the opens $T_W$ with $W\in\mathcal B$, $W\subseteq V\cap U$; on them the map lifts to arrows $(W,T_W)\to(U,S)$. Parallel arrows with equal images are equal since a poset has at most one arrow. Finally, given any etale cover $\{T_i\to T\}$ of $p(U,T)$, the vertical family $\{(U,T_i)\to(U,T)\}$ lifts it. These are exactly the cover preservation, cover lifting, local fullness, local faithfulness and density hypotheses for the comparison in the next step. Arbitrary basis intersections are covered, rather than assumed to be basis members or affine.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-dense-hypersheaf-comparison] to $p$, using all five checks in step 2. Thus hypersheaves on $B_{\mathrm{et}}$ with pointwise bound $a$ are equivalent to those on $\mathcal E$ with that bound. The inverse is concrete: extend a coherent presheaf $F$ by the homotopy right Kan extension $T\mapsto\operatorname{holim}_{(p(U,S)\to T)^{\mathrm{op}}}F(U,S)$. The lemma states both that this extension has hyperdescent and that its unit and counit are enhanced equivalences, including derived mapping complexes; an ordinary sheaf comparison alone would not establish those assertions.

source.place: Agent-written derived-section/total-site argument for the affine-local repair of the opening compactification choice.

proof.text: The full-sieve diagram in step 1 satisfies [lem-cbc-grothendieck-hypersheaf-sections]: the topology on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the topology restricted from $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, since both use exactly jointly surjective etale families over the same objects. For its local lower-refinement hypothesis, take basis opens $U,V\subseteq W$, an etale $S$ over $V$, an etale $T$ over $U$, and an arrow $S\to T$ over $W$. Its composite to $W$ factors through $U\cap V$. The inverse images $S_Z=S\times_W Z$, indexed by basis members $Z\subseteq U\cap V$, form an etale covering of $S$ in $V_{\mathrm{et}}$; each belongs to $\mathcal C_Z$ with $Z\subseteq U,V$. These verify exactly the added hypothesis, without requiring an intersection to be a basis member. Its total site is precisely $\mathcal E$ from step 2. Under the fibre restriction comparison, $F(U,T)$ becomes $F_U(T)$, the singleton identity-underlying arrows become $F_U|_V\simeq F_V$, and strings of arrows give exactly the composition and higher matching homotopies. Vertical hyperdescent is the hypersheaf condition for each $F_U$. The lemma identifies the mapping complexes with the coherent ends, including their composition, so this is the full subcategory with prescribed lower bound $a$ in the coherent basis-system category $\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ub}}(B,\mathcal B,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Compose the model equivalence on $B_{\mathrm{et}}$, the comparison of step 3, the fibre equivalence of step 4, and the inverse model equivalences on the fibres. Evaluated at $(U,T)$, this composite takes $M$ to $R\Gamma(T,M|_U)$ and then to $M|_U$; consequently its forward functor is the claimed restriction functor. Its explicit inverse takes $(M_U)$ to the fibre hypersheaves, forms their total presheaf, applies the right Kan extension from step 3, and takes the inverse derived-section model. Every operation has an enhanced inverse and preserves $a$. This proves the assertion with any fixed bound. Taking the union over integers proves the $\mathbf D^+$ assertion: for two objects choose the smaller of their lower bounds, so their complete mapping complexes already lie in one of the fixed-bound full subcategories.

proof.text: For $W\subseteq B$ use $\mathcal B_W=\{U\in\mathcal B:U\subseteq W\}$ and the identical construction over $W$. Restricting the forward functor and all its fibre evaluations gives the same $R\Gamma(T,M|_U)$ for $T\to U\subseteq W$. The slice naturality of the model, the commutative-square naturality of the dense comparison, and the index naturality of the fibre comparison identify these squares coherently. For a change of basis, compare both bases with their union, again a set and a basis; the forgetful diagrams of total sites commute, and the same three naturalities give the refinement equivalences. This argument uses arbitrary covering families, with no finite-subcover or affine-overlap assertion.

proof.text: Let $R$ denote the enhanced restriction equivalence proved above and $G$ its enhanced inverse. For any small enhanced parameter category $P$, postcomposition defines $R_*:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathbf D^+)\to\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ub}})$ and $G_*$ in the reverse direction. Whiskering the coherent unit $GR\simeq1$ and counit $RG\simeq1$ with $P$ gives inverse equivalences on these functor categories. On a simplex this is simply composition with $R$ or $G$, so it retains transformations, their composition, and every specified homotopy. An objectwise lower bound $a(p)$ suffices: each $G(F(p))$ is bounded below by that same $a(p)$; no integer bounding all parameters is used. Passing a coherent diagram to its homotopy category sends its homotopies to the asserted equations. This follows from the definitions of enhanced functors and homotopy categories, and never replaces coherent mapping ends by an equalizer of ordinary morphism groups.

tool_uses.why: Open immersions are etale, etale morphisms compose and cancel; needed to construct the etale chart site and its basis covers.
Identifies the slice etale site at an open with its own small etale site, as required by slice naturality of the hypersheaf model.
Exact inverse image for constant module coefficients preserves the prescribed cohomology lower bound. The compact-support unit has no replacement for this generic site tool.
